relevance_note: Single-patient case report of a GFAP-confirmed Alexander disease patient: "GFAP gene sequencing revealed a heterozygous missense mutation (c.197G > A, p.Arg66Gln)".
method_note: Hand-built from a full read of the paper (short case report, no tables); a Python script in scratch assembled the JSON and checked spans. Two people: 'patient' (the 82-year-old woman, first-hand) and 'unnamed person 1', an 85-year-old AxD patient from an autopsy report mentioned in the Discussion (in scope under v4 because an age and features are given). The autopsy sentence carries no citation itself; the next sentence cites (11), so the reference was not assigned (source_reference_in_review left 'not reported', label by rule 6 rather than rule 4). Its vital status 'deceased' is from the word 'autopsy'; its age 85 is recorded as age at last evaluation, deceased_age left null. Temporal change rather than a true contradiction: dysarthria and dysphagia were absent at presentation ('We observed no bulbar symptoms or signs, including dysarthria, dysphagia, or dysphonia') but developed after a minor head injury; both rows are emitted and, under the contradiction rule, checklist items 'dysphagia' and 'dysarthria or dysphonia' are set 'not reported'. Age at onset 'after the age of 80 years' is a lower bound, so no ISO duration was given; the 82-year age is age at presentation, not stated as age at diagnosis or last evaluation, so those fields are 'not reported'. Hedged findings: 'mild atrophy of the MO was suspected' recorded as observed with 'suspected' in detail; 'tadpole-like brainstem atrophy was not distinctly evident' recorded as excluded with that qualifier. Checklist composites left 'not reported' where only part was addressed: 'eye movement abnormality or diplopia' (ocular movements unremarkable; diplopia not addressed), 'hydrocephalus or raised intracranial pressure' (no ventricular enlargement; NPH only suspected; ICP not addressed). Electrodiagnostic studies were normal as a whole except prolonged CMCT; recorded as written. Periventricular WM signal changes were not called a rim, so 'periventricular rim' is 'not reported'. No treatment reported; postmortem not performed for the index patient.
